# js8call

**Weak-signal keyboard-to-keyboard messaging built on the FT8 modem**

- **Version recorded:** 3.0.3
- **Categories:** `digital-modes`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/JS8Call-improved/JS8Call-improved>
- **Needs first:** `libhamlib4t64`

## What it does

Sends and receives short text messages over HF using the same weak-signal modem technology as FT8, so contacts work at signal levels well below what voice or CW can manage.

## Why you would want it

It is the practical choice for keyboard-to-keyboard conversation and store-and-forward messaging when band conditions are poor. Where FT8 only exchanges signal reports, JS8Call carries actual text.

## Before it will work

Rig control via hamlib or flrig, and correctly routed sound-card audio between the radio and the computer.

## How it installs

- apt: `js8call` — *on linuxmint; version 22.3*
  - Mint 22.3 has Qt 6.4.2 and JS8Call 2.5.2 needs Qt 6.5. The repository version is older but it runs.
- git (cmake) — https://github.com/JS8Call-improved/JS8Call-improved at `v3.0.3`
  - build dependencies: `qt6-multimedia-dev`, `qt6-serialport-dev`, `qt6-tools-dev`, `libboost-dev`, `libfftw3-dev`, `libhamlib-dev`, `gfortran`, `cmake`, `build-essential`

Binaries this produces:

- `JS8Call` → `js8call`

## Known problems

Needs Qt 6.5 or newer. Linux Mint 22.3 ships Qt 6.4.2, so that target installs the older repository build instead. This branch is exercised in CI against a real Mint 22.3 container — the linuxmintd image ships Ubuntu's base-files, so the target build installs Mint's own base-files from Mint's repo to restore its true os-release (Q-014; see containers/Dockerfile.target IDENTITY_PACKAGE and containers/targets.yaml).

- strategy: rebuild
